stem: A client reports months of widespread pain, fatigue, poor sleep, and difficulty concentrating. No alternative inflammatory or structural diagnosis has been identified. Which condition is most consistent with this presentation?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis, an inflammatory autoimmune arthritis usually associated with objective joint inflammation and stiffness.
options.B: Normal aging, in which persistent widespread pain, fatigue, sleep disturbance, and cognitive impairment are expected findings.
options.C: An acute bacterial infection, which would more typically produce an acute systemic illness rather than months of stable symptoms.
options.D: Fibromyalgia, a chronic disorder commonly associated with widespread pain, fatigue, sleep disturbance, and cognitive symptoms.

rationale: NIAMS describes fibromyalgia as a chronic disorder characterized by widespread pain, fatigue, and trouble sleeping, with possible problems concentrating, thinking clearly, and remembering. NIAMS also notes that no specific laboratory or imaging test confirms fibromyalgia and evaluation often includes ruling out other causes. D best matches the presentation.
educational_objective: Recognize the characteristic fibromyalgia symptom cluster of chronic widespread pain, fatigue, sleep disturbance, and cognitive symptoms after evaluation for alternative causes.
source_organization: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS), NIH
source_document_title: Fibromyalgia; Fibromyalgia: Diagnosis, Treatment, and Steps to Take
source_locator: Fibromyalgia Overview/Symptoms: chronic widespread pain, fatigue, trouble sleeping, concentration/memory problems. Diagnosis: no specific laboratory or imaging test; clinicians evaluate symptoms and rule out other causes.
source_claim_supported: Fibromyalgia commonly presents with chronic widespread pain, fatigue, sleep problems and cognitive symptoms, with diagnosis based on clinical evaluation and exclusion of alternative causes rather than a single confirmatory test.

correction_summary: Retained the fibromyalgia construct and key D, linked the symptom cluster and diagnostic caveat directly to current NIAMS guidance, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.exact_locator: NIAMS Fibromyalgia Symptoms and Diagnosis sections
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses the source-supported symptom cluster and correctly avoids claiming a single confirmatory test exists.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because the vignette lacks the inflammatory joint pattern expected for RA.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because this symptom cluster is not an expected normal-aging state.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because months of stable widespread symptoms do not fit an acute bacterial illness.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D integrates the full chronic symptom cluster and exclusion context.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are possible interpretations of widespread symptoms; D is selected by the characteristic cluster.
